Strait of Hormuz Status: October 10, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  223 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
10 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.43 + 0.55 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 The Maritime Executive reports more tankers have been struck as the IRGC expands its threat against vessels it deems non-compliant with designated routes.

02 The Financial Times reports tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have surged to a wartime high and that Iran has extended attacks beyond the strait into the Gulf.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains under severe operational pressure, with The Maritime Executive reporting additional tankers struck as the IRGC broadens its threat posture against vessels it considers non-compliant. The Financial Times reports attacks have reached a wartime high and that Iran has extended strikes beyond the strait into the wider Gulf. Iranian state media, per IRNA, claim the IRGC Navy has renewed warnings to vessels attempting to pass through a restricted zone south of the strait; Latest news from Azerbaijan and The Maritime Executive separately carry related reporting on the IRGC expanding its threat against non-compliant vessels. NDTV reports an LPG tanker was struck in the Hormuz area, reported on October 9, with the IRGC claiming the vessel was taking an illegal route. A mine-strike report involving multiple tankers in the strait carries no major wire in this feed. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; a multi-day lag is expected given the weekly publication schedule. Brent stood at $104.43 as of 00:25 UTC, up 0.55% in the last session before the close; futures markets are currently shut and that figure has not changed since close. Thirty-three headlines have been indexed in the past 24 hours. The diplomatic picture remains deadlocked, with Iran's parliament speaker having said on October 4 that the strait will not open until Iran's seven conditions are met. As of 00:20 UTC, 155 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.

Cite as
Straits, “Hormuz daily brief”, 10 Oct 2026 .
